t.4.28.1: Having beheld the spotless sky, from which the lightning and the clouds had departed, resounding with the cries of sārasa cranes and anointed with lovely moonlight as with a fragrant salve…
t.4.28.2: Sugrīva, whose aims were now fulfilled, who had grown slack in pursuing righteousness and wealth, who had gone far down the path of the wicked, and whose mind was set wholly on private pleasures.
t.4.28.3: Him whose work was at an end and whose purpose was accomplished, who was ever delighting in women, and who had obtained every one of the wishes he had longed for.
t.4.28.4: Him, sporting day and night with his own beloved wife and with the longed-for Tārā as well, his purpose accomplished and his anguish gone.
t.4.28.5: He was sporting like the lord of the gods in Nandana with troops of apsarases, having entrusted his affairs to his ministers and paying no heed to those ministers.
t.4.28.7: The son of Māruta, skilled in speech, having won over the lord of the monkeys, who knew the true essence of speech, with words that were sweet, well-reasoned and delightful to the mind,
t.4.28.6: Hanumān, firm in his resolve, knowing the true essence of affairs and discerning the particular duties suited to the time, turned to the king, who had abandoned the commands of the kingdom and remained given over to a life of pleasure.
t.4.28.8: Approaching the lord of the monkeys, Hanumān spoke words that were beneficial, true and wholesome, imbued with conciliation, righteousness, purpose and sound policy, joined with affection and goodwill, and resolved through trust.
t.4.28.9: Kingship has been obtained, and fame as well, and the fortune of your lineage has been increased. What remains is the winning over of friends, and that you ought to do.
t.4.28.10: Indeed, he who, knowing the right time, always conducts himself well toward his friends, his kingdom, his fame and his majesty all increase.
t.4.28.11: O king, he whose treasury, army, allies and own self are all joined together attains and enjoys a great kingdom.
t.4.28.12: Therefore you, rich in good conduct and standing firm on the faultless path, ought to carry out properly the purpose of your friend, a purpose that is fitting and just.
t.4.28.13: But he who attends to a friend's affairs only after their proper time has passed, even if he accomplishes great things, is not credited with serving his friend's purpose.
t.4.28.14: Let this search for Vaidehī be undertaken for Rāghava. O hero, O subduer of enemies, this task of yours is already overdue.
t.4.28.15: Though he is eager to hasten, that wise one who knows the proper time does not tell you that the time has passed, O king, for he remains obedient to your will.
t.4.28.16: Rāghava is the banner of a flourishing lineage and a friend of long standing. He is of immeasurable power, and he himself is without equal in virtues.
t.4.28.17: You must indeed carry out his task, for he first accomplished yours. O lord of the monkeys, you should command the foremost of the monkeys.
t.4.28.18: Indeed, the time cannot yet have passed without any urging, for it is only in the case of a task that has been urged that there can be a lapse of the appointed time.
t.4.28.19: O lord of the monkeys, you render service even to one who has done nothing for you; how much more, then, to him who has benefited you with a kingdom and with wealth?
t.4.28.20: You are mighty and valiant, O lord of the hosts of monkeys and bears. Why then do you hesitate to give the command to accomplish what pleases Dāśarathi?
t.4.28.21: Dāśarathi is certainly able to bring the suras, asuras and great serpents under his control with his arrows, but he is waiting for you to fulfil your promise.
t.4.28.23: Neither the Devas nor the Gandharvas, neither the Asuras nor the hosts of Maruts, nor the Yakṣas could cause him fear; how much less, then, the Rākṣasas!
t.4.28.22: Unhesitating at the thought of giving up his life, he did what was dear to you. For his sake, let us search for Vaidehī both on the earth and in the sky.
t.4.28.24: Therefore, O lord of the tawny ones, you, to whom a kindness was done before, ought likewise to do with your whole being what is pleasing to Rāma, who is thus endowed with power.
t.4.28.25: O lord of the monkeys, at your command the movement of none of us is hindered, neither below on the earth, nor in the waters, nor above in the sky.
t.4.28.26: Therefore command: who is to do what for your sake, and where is he to stay? For those invincible monkeys stand before you by the crore, O sinless one.
t.4.28.27: Having heard those words of his, well spoken at the proper time, Sugrīva, endowed with strength of character, made an excellent resolve.
t.4.28.28: He instructed Nīla, whom he esteemed and who was ever diligent in his efforts, to gather together all the armies from every direction.
t.4.28.29: Act in such a way that my whole army, all the leaders of the troops, and the vanguards of the forces assemble without hindrance.
t.4.28.30: Let those monkeys who guard the frontiers, swift-moving and resolute, quickly assemble the army at my command; and thereafter you yourself should review the army.
t.4.28.31: Any vānara who does not arrive here within fifteen nights shall suffer the punishment of death; on this there is to be no deliberation.
t.4.28.32: "Let you, together with Aṅgada, go to the elder monkeys, taking charge of my firm command." Having made this arrangement, the mighty lord of the foremost monkeys entered his dwelling.
